summary.title: Build Your Own Database From Scratch in Go
summary.one_liner: You learn how a database works from the bottom up by building a B+tree key-value store in Go, adding durability, then transactions and a SQL-like query layer.
takeaways: Build a B+tree data structure for querying and manipulating data, the core of a key-value store.
Make the store durable with crash recovery, the step that separates a database from a plain file.
Add tables, range queries, secondary indexes and atomic transactions on top of a copy-on-write B+tree KV store.
Finish with concurrency control and a SQL-like query language and parser.
summary.summary: This tutorial book walks through building a database in simple Golang code, in small steps. Part I (free web version) covers files versus databases, indexing structures, B-tree and crash recovery, B+tree node insertion and deletion, an append-only KV store, and a free list for reuse. Part II, available in the ebook and paperback editions, adds tables on KV, range queries, secondary indexes, atomic transactions, concurrency control, a SQL parser, and a query language. The page also recommends Database Internals, Designing Data-Intensive Applications, and the Go-based trialofcode course that uses an LSM-Tree instead.
